Akron Zips.status: Transfer — arriving via North Texas, having previously been at Miami (FL) and Albany.
Akron Zips.previous_school: North Texas; previously Miami (FL) and Albany.
Akron Zips.career_experience: Originally recruited to Miami (FL) after a strong season at Albany; held a clipboard for Cam Ward at Miami in 2024 and for Drew Mestemaker at North Texas in 2025.
Akron Zips.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a count.
Akron Zips.passing: 14 total passes across the last two seasons.
Akron Zips.competition: The guide describes minimal resistance for the job.
Akron Zips.author_confidence: Positive about the situation rather than the résumé. What the guide likes is what he inherits, not what he has done.
Akron Zips.positive_case: Minimal resistance for the job, a head coach who was a longtime coordinator and quarterbacks coach, a 1,000-yard rusher in Jordan Gant representing genuine growth in the run game, and returning pass-catchers including leading receiver Marcel Williams.
Akron Zips.concerns: He has barely played — 14 passes across two seasons.
Akron Zips.scheme_fit: Joe Moorhead was a longtime coordinator and quarterbacks coach before taking this job, which the guide treats as the developmental asset.
Akron Zips.supporting_cast: Better than usual for Akron: a 1,000-yard rusher in Jordan Gant and returning pass-catchers including Marcel Williams. Up front the guide tracks improvement — 63 sacks allowed in 2021 and 56 in 2022, improving to 30 in 2024 and 35 in 2025, with last year's -9 sack differential easily the best in a very long time.
Akron Zips.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 4.5 wins. The single data point the guide finds most impressive is a 19-16 road win at Bowling Green immediately after an overtime loss to rival Kent State. Its conclusion is that this was possibly a better team than 5-7 suggested and that Moorhead is finally gaining ground. Projection is 4.29 wins, with a stated liking for the team.
Akron Zips.outlook_dependency: Moderate. The guide's Over rests on programme trajectory and a corrected reading of last season rather than on quarterback play.

Ball State Cardinals.status: New starter, identity undetermined — the guide answers its own question literally, saying somebody must start, without naming who.
Ball State Cardinals.previous_school: Keldric Luster comes via Texas State, previously SMU; Tyler Mizzell from Concord, previously Wake Forest.
Ball State Cardinals.career_experience: Luster barely played across two years at SMU and again at Texas State; Mizzell threw 10 interceptions with 26 touchdown passes for Division II Concord after leaving Wake Forest; Khalel Wright is a redshirt freshman from Uremovich's first class; Mason Adkins is this year's top true freshman recruit.
Ball State Cardinals.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as counts.
Ball State Cardinals.passing: Mizzell threw 26 touchdowns against 10 interceptions at Division II Concord; the others' production is not addressed. The 2025 starting quarterback threw for just 1,583 yards.
Ball State Cardinals.rushing: Quarterback Kiael Kelly led the team with just 600 rushing yards at 2.8 per carry.
Ball State Cardinals.efficiency: Team-level: 15.8 PPG and 4.5 yards per play.
Ball State Cardinals.turnovers: Mizzell's 10 interceptions at Division II are the only figure given.
Ball State Cardinals.competition: Open among four named candidates — Keldric Luster, Tyler Mizzell, Khalel Wright and Mason Adkins — with the guide naming no favourite.
Ball State Cardinals.backup: The four named candidates are Luster, Mizzell, Wright and Adkins.
Ball State Cardinals.author_confidence: Very low. The guide says there is no clear evidence any of them can be an FBS-level starter, even in the MAC.
Ball State Cardinals.positive_case: Not addressed in guide for any candidate.
Ball State Cardinals.concerns: An exceedingly low baseline — 15.8 PPG, 4.5 yards per play, 49 sacks allowed and a starting quarterback who threw for just 1,583 yards — which the guide still concludes is unlikely to move much higher.
Ball State Cardinals.scheme_fit: Uremovich is his own play-caller, and the guide is direct that last year's results were pathetic.
Ball State Cardinals.supporting_cast: Almost nothing. Returning production is one rushing touchdown and two receiving. Quarterback Kiael Kelly led the team with just 600 rushing yards at 2.8 per carry, Qian Magwood led receivers with 19 catches for 320 yards, and returnee Donovan Hamilton had 20 for 244. The guide allows the offensive line might be better.
Ball State Cardinals.portal_context: Ball State has next to no returning production, so Uremovich starts Year 2 with essentially a brand-new roster; the guide allows he may prefer his own portal class and two freshman classes to what he inherited.
Ball State Cardinals.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 3.5 wins, which the guide itself calls a tepid take at best. Its reason for the hedge: even with 16 PPG in conference play the Cardinals still won three of those eight games, plus the win over FCS New Hampshire. Two of the three most winnable conference games are road trips to Kent State and UMass. Projection is 3.41 wins.
Ball State Cardinals.outlook_dependency: High. The guide's assessment of the offense — and therefore the season — is built on the quarterback bar not moving.
Ball State Cardinals.conflicts: The guide names four candidates and declines to state an expected starter, so this record carries no VSiN preseason expectation for the position.

Bowling Green Falcons.status: Undetermined — the guide states the position remains in flux.
Bowling Green Falcons.previous_school: Not addressed in guide for 2026 candidates. Drew Pyne arrived via Notre Dame and Missouri.
Bowling Green Falcons.career_experience: Not addressed in guide for 2026 candidates.
Bowling Green Falcons.passing: Four quarterbacks saw action last season and collectively produced as many touchdowns as interceptions, 12 apiece.
Bowling Green Falcons.efficiency: Team-level: 20.5 PPG and 4.9 yards per play.
Bowling Green Falcons.turnovers: 12 interceptions against 12 touchdowns from the quarterback group.
Bowling Green Falcons.competition: Unresolved. The guide states the position remains in flux and leaves a counterfactual open rather than resolving it: nobody will know whether things would have gone better had Drew Pyne not been hurt.
Bowling Green Falcons.backup: Not addressed in guide by name for 2026.
Bowling Green Falcons.author_confidence: Low. The guide names very little on offense, especially through the air, as one of the specific failures of last season.
Bowling Green Falcons.positive_case: The major silver lining it identifies is timing rather than personnel: George and his staff could work the portal alongside everyone else this cycle, rather than in March last year after he was hired.
Bowling Green Falcons.concerns: Four quarterbacks used, a 12-to-12 touchdown-to-interception ratio, and a position still in flux.
Bowling Green Falcons.scheme_fit: Not addressed in guide at quarterback; the guide notes the scheme uses a lot of 12 personnel.
Bowling Green Falcons.supporting_cast: Clarified rather than strengthened. The guide reads last season as fact-finding missions to identify who fits: Austyn Dendy looks like the feature back after a solid freshman season at 4.6 yards per carry, and it expects a tighter rotation with Charleston Southern transfer Ke'Marion Baldwin, who averaged nearly five yards per carry. Players who appeared without being focal points now get chances at receiver, on the line and at tight end.
Bowling Green Falcons.portal_context: The staff could work the portal on the normal cycle for the first time; Ke'Marion Baldwin arrives from Charleston Southern.
Bowling Green Falcons.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 4.5 wins, explicitly not a bet given the heavy vig. The guide expects most wins to come in conference, because non-conference brings Nebraska, Iowa State and South Florida. Its tactical suggestion is to wait for the market: the schedule softens considerably after that stretch, so an in-season win total on Bowling Green after a likely 1-4 start might be the way to go. Projection is 4.26 wins.
Bowling Green Falcons.outlook_dependency: High. The guide names offensive failure, especially through the air, as one of the two specific causes of last season's disappointments.
Bowling Green Falcons.conflicts: The guide states the position is in flux and names no 2026 candidates, so this record carries no VSiN preseason expectation for the position.

Buffalo Bulls.status: New starter, identity undetermined — the guide calls this by far the most questionable position group on the roster.
Buffalo Bulls.previous_school: Elijah Holmes comes from Division II Wingate; Jason Wright and Qur'an McNeill are in-house.
Buffalo Bulls.career_experience: Holmes threw for over 3,000 yards for Wingate; redshirt freshman Jason Wright had 15 rushing attempts and no pass attempts; Qur'an McNeill is a true freshman.
Buffalo Bulls.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as counts.
Buffalo Bulls.passing: Holmes threw for over 3,000 yards at Division II Wingate; Wright has no pass attempts.
Buffalo Bulls.turnovers: Not addressed in guide for the candidates; team-level, Buffalo swung 16 in turnover margin from +9 to -7.
Buffalo Bulls.competition: Open. The guide's own expectation is that true freshman Qur'an McNeill plays sooner rather than later, reasoning from his offer list — Arkansas, Cincinnati, UConn, Syracuse and Boston College — that a programme with a very light NIL budget invested heavily to land him.
Buffalo Bulls.backup: The named candidates are Elijah Holmes, Jason Wright and Qur'an McNeill.
Buffalo Bulls.author_confidence: Low. The guide calls this by far the most questionable position group on the roster.
Buffalo Bulls.positive_case: McNeill's offer list is the guide's stated evidence of real talent; Holmes brings Division II production.
Buffalo Bulls.concerns: The guide uses last season as proof of the position's primacy: Buffalo excelled on special teams and played well on defense, but Ta'Quan Roberson could not match what C.J. Ogbonna had done the year before, and the turnover margin swung 16 as a result.
Buffalo Bulls.supporting_cast: Weakened. Two players with 62 receptions apiece are gone, as is Al-Jay Henderson, who fell from a 1,000-yard rusher to 755 yards because of attrition up front.
Buffalo Bulls.portal_context: Holmes arrives from Division II Wingate; the guide notes Buffalo has a very light NIL budget.
Buffalo Bulls.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 6.5 wins, described as a price play because the juice on Over 5.5 is cost-prohibitive, even though 6-6 looks like the most likely outcome. Its schedule case is favourable, and it flags one eligibility mechanic as a motivating factor: with two FCS games on the slate, Buffalo needs seven wins for a bowl unless a waiver allows six with two FCS wins among them. Projection is 6.32 wins.
Buffalo Bulls.outlook_dependency: Very high. The guide explicitly argues the position is where last season was decided, since the other phases held up.
Buffalo Bulls.conflicts: The guide names three candidates and declines to state an expected starter, so this record carries no VSiN preseason expectation for the position.

Central Michigan Chippewas.status: Returning — the mobile quarterback the guide describes Drinkall as building his 21-personnel plan around.
Central Michigan Chippewas.career_experience: The team's second-leading rusher and top touchdown-scorer last season.
Central Michigan Chippewas.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a count.
Central Michigan Chippewas.rushing: 107 carries; second-leading rusher and top touchdown-scorer on the team.
Central Michigan Chippewas.efficiency: Not addressed in guide for Flores; Joe Labas completed 70.6% with a 13-to-6 ratio.
Central Michigan Chippewas.turnovers: Not addressed in guide for Flores; Labas threw six interceptions against 13 touchdowns.
Central Michigan Chippewas.competition: Effectively a shared role last season, and the guide does not resolve it for 2026: Labas completed 70.6% with a 13-to-6 ratio while Flores was the running quarterback with 107 carries against just 28 pass attempts.
Central Michigan Chippewas.backup: Joe Labas, the passing half of last season's split.
Central Michigan Chippewas.author_confidence: Positive about the scheme rather than about a named quarterback. The guide's framing device is a recruiting pitch: a quarterback who would rather run than throw should consider Central Michigan while Drinkall is still there.
Central Michigan Chippewas.positive_case: Flores fits the intended identity — heavy 21 personnel with a mobile quarterback — and the guide argues that in a conference this inefficient, shortening the game and limiting possessions may be extremely fruitful.
Central Michigan Chippewas.concerns: The scheme is not yet installed: the offense averaged only 3.9 yards per carry, not what Drinkall's Army history would suggest, and the personnel are hard to find because spread and run-and-gun styles are in vogue.
Central Michigan Chippewas.scheme_fit: Central to the whole record. Drinkall is looking to run a lot of 21 personnel with a mobile quarterback, supported by many returning linemen and some portal additions, and the guide reads leading receiver Langston Lewis staying as meaningful evidence of buy-in.
Central Michigan Chippewas.supporting_cast: Fit for purpose. Brock Townsend averaged over five yards per carry and Vaughn Blue did the same at Liberty. On the line the guide turns an apparent weakness into intent: the group is slightly undersized by design, because the linemen must pull and get out ahead of plays. Its verdict is that they are very, very close.
Central Michigan Chippewas.portal_context: Some portal additions on the offensive line; Vaughn Blue arrives from Liberty.
Central Michigan Chippewas.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 6.5 wins. Its conference-wide evidence comes from Brian Fremeau at BCF Toys: not a single MAC team ranked in the top 50 in Offensive Points Per Drive. On the schedule it notes the conference draw is a bit tougher, but the Chippewas host Sacramento State and play only three true conference road games. Projection is 6.14 wins.
Central Michigan Chippewas.outlook_dependency: High. The Over is built on the ground-and-pound identity working, which the guide describes in quarterback terms.
Central Michigan Chippewas.conflicts: The guide names Flores as the mobile quarterback the scheme is built around while separately presenting last season as a split with Joe Labas and asking how close Drinkall is to running the offense he wants. It does not state which starts in 2026.

Eastern Michigan Eagles.previous_school: Michigan State — a Class of 2020 commit there.
Eastern Michigan Eagles.career_experience: In his seventh season of college football.
Eastern Michigan Eagles.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a count.
Eastern Michigan Eagles.passing: An 18-to-11 touchdown-to-interception ratio with a MAC-leading 2,817 passing yards.
Eastern Michigan Eagles.rushing: Not addressed in guide as production; the guide credits him with enough mobility to evade pressure.
Eastern Michigan Eagles.efficiency: Not addressed in guide as a completion rate; the guide notes the offense produced only 24.1 PPG despite allowing just 11 sacks.
Eastern Michigan Eagles.competition: None described — Kim is the settled starter.
Eastern Michigan Eagles.author_confidence: Neutral. The guide reads Eastern Michigan through continuity rather than through the quarterback's ceiling.
Eastern Michigan Eagles.positive_case: MAC-leading passing yardage, mobility to evade pressure, and continuity: per Bill Connelly, Eastern Michigan ranks 24th in percentage of returning production, and per Phil Steele the Eagles are No. 1 in the MAC and No. 7 nationally in his experience chart.
Eastern Michigan Eagles.concerns: Only 24.1 PPG despite excellent protection, and the guide leaves one figure deliberately unresolved: Eastern Michigan went from 5.1 to 5.7 yards per play between 2024 and 2025 yet scored 1.8 fewer points per game.
Eastern Michigan Eagles.supporting_cast: Mixed. 1,000-yard rusher Dontae McMillan is gone and was also the second-leading receiver, but the guide expects production from Braydon Bennett, who averaged over six yards per carry at Coastal Carolina, plus the depth backs. Its overall read is a largely similar offense with a less experienced offensive line.
Eastern Michigan Eagles.portal_context: The lowest-ranked portal class in the conference per 247Sports, but a freshman class tied for the largest — which the guide reads as a deliberate development philosophy that is a hard route nowadays.
Eastern Michigan Eagles.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 5.5 wins, on the judgement that the roster's talent level does not seem any stronger. It sets the whole case against the era: other programmes appear to be evolving more, and portal success seems paramount now. A bowl is possible, but the ceiling is probably six wins. Projection is 5.39 wins.
Eastern Michigan Eagles.outlook_dependency: Moderate. The guide's Under is argued from roster-building philosophy and schedule, with the quarterback part of the continuity it is testing.

Kent State Golden Flashes.status: Returning starter — a redshirt freshman in 2025.
Kent State Golden Flashes.career_experience: Came basically out of nowhere last season as a redshirt freshman after finally keeping his ACL intact.
Kent State Golden Flashes.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a count.
Kent State Golden Flashes.passing: An 18-to-3 touchdown-to-interception ratio with just over 2,000 passing yards.
Kent State Golden Flashes.efficiency: Not addressed in guide as a rate; the guide says the yardage totals still were not eye-popping even in conference play, locating the gain instead in taking care of the football and protecting the quarterback.
Kent State Golden Flashes.turnovers: Only three interceptions as the primary quarterback — though Kent State was still negative in turnover margin.
Kent State Golden Flashes.competition: None described — DeShields is the settled starter.
Kent State Golden Flashes.backup: None with FBS experience; the guide calls this dependency massive.
Kent State Golden Flashes.author_confidence: Positive on production, alarmed about depth. The guide's first point on the rest of the offense is that DeShields staying healthy is vital because there is absolutely no FBS experience behind him.
Kent State Golden Flashes.positive_case: An 18-to-3 ratio that took Kent State over 20 PPG for the first time since 2022, achieved after top receivers Chrishon McCray and Luke Floriea moved on having combined for 84 of the team's 139 receptions the previous year.
Kent State Golden Flashes.concerns: Health, with nothing behind him, and a supporting cast stripped again — the top four rushers are gone along with the top two receivers by yardage.
Kent State Golden Flashes.scheme_fit: Not addressed in guide; the guide notes a more stable passing game and a full recruiting cycle for Mark Carney should help.
Kent State Golden Flashes.supporting_cast: Thin. Wayne Harris — 35 receptions for only 383 yards — is the leading returnee; the receiver room took in few new faces while virtually the entire running back room is new. On the line the guide allows the group may be better despite lost starters, since it helped produce only 2.9 yards per carry overall and 3.6 in conference games once the brutal non-conference schedule is excluded.
Kent State Golden Flashes.portal_context: A fascinating age split on defense — portal seniors alongside homegrown sophomores; the receiver room took in few new faces.
Kent State Golden Flashes.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 3.5 wins, though the guide expects matching last season's five wins to be a challenge. Its swing game is the finale at Eastern Michigan, an opponent it is very low on. It calls this not a super strong play while noting the talent level is better again, adds Josh Cribbs as the new special teams coordinator as a possible X factor, and states it likes the position despite a projection of 3.23 wins.
Kent State Golden Flashes.outlook_dependency: Very high, and specifically on availability. The guide calls the dependency on DeShields' health massive.
